clue.text: With bird about, remove car

indicators.note: the bird is placed about, that is around, the word for remove

parts.note: a jay is a bird of the crow family
to lop is to cut off or remove

explanation.surface: Someone is told to take the car away while a bird hovers about.
explanation.definitionFit: A jalopy is an old, battered motor vehicle, so it is a kind of car.

clue.text: Dance movement involves method and craft

indicators.note: to involve is to take in, so the dance step wraps round the method

parts.note: a jeté is a ballet leap, a dance movement
a plan is a method or scheme

explanation.surface: A choreographer explains that a dance routine needs both technique and craft.
explanation.definitionFit: A jet plane is an aircraft, and craft is a general word for vessels including aircraft.

clue.text: Early on, lots of blue sky

indicators.note: the earliest letter of each of the next three words is taken

explanation.surface: In the morning there is plenty of clear blue sky.
explanation.definitionFit: To sky a ball is to hit it high in the air, which is what a lob does; both are verbs.

clue.text: Bullfighter craving diamonds and gold

parts.note: pica is a medical term for a craving to eat non-food substances
D is the card-game abbreviation for the suit of diamonds
or is the heraldic word for gold

explanation.surface: A greedy matador hankers after jewels and treasure.
explanation.definitionFit: A picador is the mounted bullfighter who goads the bull with a lance.

clue.text: Bill and Teddy drew attention

parts.note: a bill is a poster or advertisement, an advert
Ed is a short form of the name Edward, like Teddy

explanation.surface: Two friends named Bill and Teddy pointed something out.
explanation.walkthrough: Bill and Teddy look like two names, but only Teddy is a name here; Bill is a poster.
explanation.definitionFit: To advert to something is to refer to it or turn attention towards it, a formal verb.

clue.text: Absorb a lot of water? Alcohol, rather

definitions.text: Absorb a lot of water? Alcohol, rather

parts.words: Absorb a lot of water? Alcohol, rather
parts.note: the first reading pictures a creature in the sea gulping water; the correction says the liquid is booze, giving an idiom for heavy drinking

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes someone who habitually consumes large amounts of alcohol, as fish seem to swallow water constantly.

clue.text: Old flame can get taken to court and wiped out

parts.note: an ex is a former partner, an old flame
a tin is a can

explanation.surface: A former lover and a tin can end up in a court case and are ruined.
explanation.definitionFit: A species that is extinct has been wiped out, with no living members remaining.

clue.text: Get worried, moving over British river crossing

indicators.note: the rearranged letters are placed over, that is around, the abbreviation for British
the letters of the words get worried are moved about into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone becomes anxious about a British bridge crossing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moving' rearranges GET WORRIED into TOWERRIDGE, and 'over' wraps those letters round B. Tower Bridge is the famous bascule bridge over the Thames in London.
explanation.definitionFit: Tower Bridge carries a road across the River Thames, so it is a river crossing.

clue.text: Knock clear into the river

indicators.note: the word for clear is put into the name of the river

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Scotland, and another in Wales and England
to rid is to clear away

explanation.surface: Someone knocks a ball clear into the river.
explanation.definitionFit: To knock something informally means to criticise or belittle it, which is what deriding does.

clue.text: Arabs, for instance, receive free rein in Check tod calm areas

clue.text: He sells packs of basic cotton for spinning

indicators.note: spinning turns the cotton about, so its letters are whirled into a new order

explanation.surface: A trader deals in bundles of plain cotton for the spinning mill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'packs' suggests bales of cotton, but here they are packets of cigarettes.
explanation.definitionFit: A tobacconist is a shopkeeper selling cigarettes, sold in packs, along with cigars and pipe tobacco.

clue.text: Mark's withdrawn from heated conflict

indicators.note: the mark is taken away from the word meaning heated; the reversed run of letters inside the word withdrawn is a coincidence

parts.note: warm means heated
M is the abbreviation for the German mark, a former currency

explanation.surface: A mark is removed from a fierce dispute.
explanation.definitionFit: A war is an armed conflict between nations or groups.

clue.text: Do rules get broken in place of pilgrimage?

indicators.note: broken pieces are reassembled, so the letters are put together in a new order

explanation.surface: A question whether regulations are flouted at a shrine.
explanation.definitionFit: Lourdes, a town in south-west France, draws millions of Catholic pilgrims to the grotto of Bernadette's visions.

clue.text: Lisper's erroneous description of minute. Titanic — it's out of the question

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held reads 'Lisper's erroneous description of minute. Titanic — it's out of the question': a lisped UNSINKABLE is plain, but 'minute.' has no job and looks like OCR garble; the scan is blank and a search found no original text.
annotationWithheld.clue: Lisper's erroneous description of minute. Titanic — it's out of the question

clue.text: Relations are cordial with communist

parts.note: kind means warm and cordial
a red is a communist

explanation.surface: Family ties are friendly despite a Marxist in the house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cordial' tempts as a drink, but here it is an adjective meaning friendly.
explanation.definitionFit: Kindred means one's relatives or family, the people related to you.

clue.text: Science, hard one, in uncomplicated narrative

indicators.note: the two pieces are set in the phrase, between its words

parts.note: natural means simple and uncomplicated
a story is a narrative
H is the pencil-grading abbreviation for hard
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A tough scientific subject is explained in a simple tale.
explanation.definitionFit: Natural history is the scientific study of plants and animals in their surroundings.

clue.text: Curious new trap set up by poet

indicators.note: in a down clue set up means the pieces are read upwards, reversing them

parts.note: nosy means curious or inquisitive
a net is a trap

explanation.surface: An inquisitive new snare was laid by a poet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set up' turns the whole run NOSYNNET backwards. Alfred, Lord Tennyson was Queen Victoria's Poet Laureate.
explanation.definitionFit: Tennyson was a celebrated Victorian poet, author of In Memoriam and The Charge of the Light Brigade.

clue.text: Who got roast beef in the game?

definitions.text: Who got roast beef in the game?

parts.words: Who got roast beef in the game?
parts.note: the toe-counting rhyme has five little piggies, and the third, in the centre, had roast beef; the answer is also a ball game

explanation.walkthrough: In the nursery rhyme 'This little piggy', the middle toe of five is the piggy that had roast beef. The answer is also a children's game where one player tries to catch a ball thrown over their head.
explanation.definitionFit: The middle of five toy pigs got roast beef, and the phrase is also a playground ball game with a player in the centre.

clue.text: Pressing chore

definitions.meaning: pressing clothes means smoothing them with a hot iron
a chore is a dull household task, like smoothing the laundry

explanation.definitionFit: Pressing clothes with a hot iron is what the word names, and it is a familiar household chore.

clue.text: Deduce number in hell

parts.note: to infer is to deduce

explanation.surface: A puzzle of working out a figure in the underworld.
explanation.definitionFit: Inferno is Italian for hell, the title of the first part of Dante's Divine Comedy.

clue.text: Fighter infiltrating before he was driven out The Times of the country

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held reads 'Fighter infiltrating before he was driven out The Times of the country': MIG inside ERE is plain, but 'The Times' is a stray page header in the OCR splitting the definition; the scan is blank and a search found no original text.
annotationWithheld.clue: Fighter infiltrating before he was driven out The Times of the country

clue.text: Pretend to understand

definitions.meaning: to pretend can mean to claim or allege falsely, as in 'he made out he was ill'
to understand is to grasp or decipher, as in barely making out the words

explanation.definitionFit: To make out can mean to claim falsely, and also to discern or grasp something.

clue.text: Team pay to receive one newspaper before noon

indicators.note: the earlier part comes before the abbreviation for noon
the payment takes in, or receives, the other pieces

parts.note: a fee is a payment
I is the Roman numeral for one
FT is the Financial Times, a British newspaper

explanation.surface: A sports side pays to get a single paper delivered before midday.
explanation.definitionFit: A rugby union team has fifteen players, so the number names the side.

clue.text: Returning to kill rabbit

indicators.note: returning means the word is read back the other way

parts.note: to bag game is to kill it in hunting

explanation.surface: A hunter goes back to shoot a rabbit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rabbit' looks like the prey, but it is the definition: in British slang to rabbit is to chatter, from rhyming slang 'rabbit and pork' for talk.
explanation.definitionFit: Rabbit is British slang for talk idly, and gab also means chatter, both verbs.

clue.text: Busy studio is run in novel fashion

indicators.note: doing something in a novel fashion means in a new way, so the letters take a new order

explanation.surface: A hectic studio is managed in an innovative way.
explanation.definitionFit: Industrious means hard-working and diligent, constantly busy.

clue.text: Left over, like 22? Yes and no!

definitions.meaning: an item left over after pairing is spare, like a single sock
the number 22 is even, but the answer at 22 across is fifteen, which is not even

explanation.definitionFit: A spare item left over is called odd, and 15 is an odd number while 22 itself is even.

clue.text: Motivate determined greenies

indicators.note: the letters are determined afresh, settled into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Resolute environmental campaigners inspire others to act.
explanation.definitionFit: To energise people is to fill them with energy and enthusiasm, that is, to motivate them.

clue.text: String along fruit tree

parts.note: cord is thin string
on can mean along, as in moving on

explanation.surface: A gardener ties a fruit tree up with twine.
explanation.definitionFit: A cordon is a fruit tree trained to grow as a single stem, often against a wall.
